content.user_title: Review Testing Strategy and Test Quality
content.value_statement: Poor test plans miss important behavior and create brittle suites. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code review tests, choose frameworks, and focus coverage on valuable user flows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use unit, integration, and end-to-end tests.
Recommends Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright, pytest, and go test by stack.
Identifies common test anti-patterns such as over-mocking and brittle selectors.
Suggests behavior-focused test questions for code reviews and mentoring.
Provides Arrange, Act, Assert structure and naming guidance for test cases.
limitations: It does not run tests or inspect runtime results by itself.
It focuses on testing strategy, not full security or performance review.
Framework recommendations are concise and may need project-specific adjustment.
It gives examples, but it does not generate complete test suites for every stack.

use_cases.title: Coach Test Planning
use_cases.description: Guide junior developers through valuable test coverage, edge cases, and review questions.

use_cases.title: Review Frontend Tests
use_cases.description: Evaluate React tests for behavior focus, semantic queries, and balanced mocking.

use_cases.title: Set Release Coverage
use_cases.description: Choose high-value unit, integration, and E2E tests before shipping a feature.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Test File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use testing-fundamentals to review this test file for behavior focus, brittle selectors, and missing edge cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing test file

prompt_templates.title: Create a Coverage Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use testing-fundamentals to create a test plan for this feature. Separate unit, integration, and end-to-end coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Brittle Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use testing-fundamentals to improve this test suite. Reduce over-mocking and keep tests focused on user-visible behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use testing-fundamentals to audit our testing strategy for this release. Identify coverage gaps, framework fit, and high-value E2E flows.

output_examples.input: Review a login form test suite that only checks successful login.
output: Calls out missing invalid password, network failure, and loading states.
Recommends behavior-focused assertions and one Playwright path for the critical login journey.

output_examples.input: Create a test strategy for a Vite React checkout feature.
output: Suggests unit tests for price calculations and validation rules.
Adds integration tests for form submission and API error handling.
Limits E2E coverage to checkout success and payment failure paths.

output_examples.input: Improve tests that use class selectors and large snapshots.
output: Replaces brittle selectors with role and label based queries.
Reduces snapshot use and asks for assertions tied to user-visible behavior.

best_practices: Prioritize tests that prove important user behavior and failure states.
Keep most coverage in fast unit tests, then add integration and E2E tests for key flows.
Mock external boundaries, but keep business logic and component behavior real when practical.
anti_patterns: Do not chase 100 percent coverage with low-value tests.
Do not test framework internals or third-party libraries.
Do not rely on CSS classes, large snapshots, or internal state for assertions.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Vitest, Jest, React Testing Library, Playwright, pytest, and go test at a strategy level.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing guidance. Any test execution must be requested through the active coding tool.

faq.question: Can it help with backend testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes general unit testing principles and mentions Node.js, Python, and Go testing tools.

faq.question: Does it replace project-specific test conventions?
faq.answer: No. Use it with the existing framework, commands, naming rules, and team standards in the repository.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What kind of review does it perform best?
faq.answer: It works best for behavior-focused review, test pyramid balance, mocking choices, and missing edge cases.
